s-run: true reproduction run, final method FIN3 (bsgP, 9972a56d): the paper's 1-D IC as is (F<sub>r</sub> = 0 above r<sub>photo</sub>), 20–80 R<sub>☉</sub>, 10<sup>−6</sup> temperature seed in 37.5–45.2 R<sub>☉</sub> (radiation in equilibrium with it), no well-balanced scheme (full M1 radiation force), Ma zero-contact inner ghosts, Ma outflow top, no flux surgery, no sponge, vet_gd closure (rotated every 1750 s, slope-corrected, averaged over the last 4 rotated sets), hesdirk2 time integration, conservative2 gas source; 4 Raven nodes, 16 A100, 16 MeshBlocks (1 per GPU)
s-banner: The run is at day 20.6 of 57.4. It is in its start-up transient: it starts, like the paper, from the radiative-only 1-D profile, which is out of thermal and hydrostatic balance, and the paper calls its envelope steady only after 30 d, so every panel on our side is still transient. Convection has developed from the seed: KE<sub>int</sub> fell to 2.5×10<sup>39</sup> erg at 7.3 d, grew to a peak of 1.4×10<sup>42</sup> erg at 10.7 d and is 1.1×10<sup>42</sup> erg now, about 0.11 of the paper's ~10<sup>43</sup> erg. From the 10<sup>−6</sup> seed, lateral motion has appeared: the lateral share of KE<sub>int</sub> is 5.2e-01 now (largest so far 5.3e-01). At 40.6 R<sub>☉</sub> convective flows have developed (v<sub>r</sub> -86.2 to +42.0 km/s). The 3D photosphere has moved from 53.0 to 53.2 R<sub>☉</sub>.
n-fig2: Energies are sums over our wedge (π/3 sr), as in the paper's appendix. M<sub>env</sub> is the whole-star equivalent of the wedge mass, 0.175 M<sub>☉</sub> for 20–80 R<sub>☉</sub> (the paper's domain). Colour maps have one column per 0.5-d snapshot and are drawn to 65 R<sub>☉</sub> like the paper's. So far ΔE<sub>grav</sub> = -5.4×10<sup>43</sup> erg, ΔU = 5.3×10<sup>43</sup> erg and E<sub>k</sub> = 1.1×10<sup>42</sup> erg (paper: about 5×10<sup>44</sup> and 10<sup>43</sup> erg in its transient). The 3D photosphere is at 50.9–60.0 R<sub>☉</sub>; the IC's is at 52.9 R<sub>☉</sub>.
n-fig3: P<sub>rad</sub> = D<sub>rr</sub>E, the Eddington tensor the vet_gd closure used, from the m1_vet dump of the same time. The right panel is the paper's IC as run: radiative only (F<sub>MLT</sub> = 0), so it has no convective shell to shade, where the paper's panel marks the two MESA convection zones. Its Fe opacity peak is at 41.4 R<sub>☉</sub> (κ<sub>R</sub> = 1.59 cm<sup>2</sup> g<sup>−1</sup>, κ/κ<sub>Edd</sub> = 0.89 with κ<sub>Edd</sub> = 4πcGM/L = 1.79), not at the 35 R<sub>☉</sub> the paper quotes. At 20.59 d the shell-mean Fe peak is at 40.4 R<sub>☉</sub> (κ<sub>R</sub> = 1.63); the He II bump near 50.6 R<sub>☉</sub> (T ≈ 4×10<sup>4</sup> K) reaches κ<sub>R</sub> = 1.18. Largest κ/κ<sub>Edd</sub> in the plane: 1.15. Largest ram/total pressure below the photosphere: 4.7 (paper: about 0.5 above 33 R<sub>☉</sub> in steady state). Opacities: Linhao Ma's TOPS tables (padded with the edge values), the tables the run uses.
n-fig4: The shell stays at 40.6 R<sub>☉</sub> (nearest cell 40.59), as on the earlier reproduction page. The paper puts it 1 R<sub>☉</sub> above its Fe peak (35 → 36 R<sub>☉</sub>); in this run the shell-mean Fe peak is at 40.4 R<sub>☉</sub> at 20.59 d, so 40.6 lies 0.2 R<sub>☉</sub> above it. At 20.59 d: v<sub>r</sub> from -86.185 to +41.982 km/s; shell means ρ = 4.77×10<sup>−8</sup> g cm<sup>−3</sup> and T = 1.712×10<sup>5</sup> K (paper, steady: 5–8×10<sup>−8</sup>, 1.5–1.7×10<sup>5</sup> K). v<sub>r</sub> uses the paper's range (±60 km/s) once our flows reach 5 % of it, else our own; ρ and T are absolute values with a fixed range = shell mean of the newest dump ± a relative amplitude (1–99th percentile, at least 0.1 %, so round-off is not painted as structure).
n-fig6: Normalised as the paper's eq. 8: the wedge luminosity (L<sub>top</sub>, the Marshak top face) is linearly detrended and its fluctuation scaled by √(Ω/4π) = 0.289 to a whole-star equivalent. Both panels use (ΔF/F)<sup>2</sup>/µHz and the paper's axis range. Our flux spans 0.910–1.188 over 0.01–20.59 d; mean whole-star L<sub>top</sub> = 5.6×10<sup>38</sup> erg/s (IC: 5.58×10<sup>38</sup>). The dotted line marks our Nyquist frequency (hst every 962 s). Before 30 d the whole curve is the start-up transient (the window falls back to the full record), so the orange "radial mode" fit is not meaningful yet.
n-int: At 20.59 d, F<sub>r</sub> is taken at each column's own τ<sub>R</sub> = 1 cell, at 51.52–54.18 R<sub>☉</sub> (1st–99th percentile; median 52.93). There F<sub>r</sub>/⟨F<sub>r</sub>⟩ spans 0.178–3.505 (rms 0.296; F<sub>r</sub> < 0 in 0.00 % of the columns), ⟨T<sub>eff</sub>⟩ = 15517 K and 4π⟨r<sup>2</sup>F<sub>r</sub>⟩ = 5.6×10<sup>38</sup> erg/s = 0.997 L.
n-ke: KE<sub>int</sub> is column 11 of user.hst (gas kinetic energy inside r<sub>int</sub>, summed over the wedge); KEr<sub>int</sub> (column 12) is its radial part, so KE<sub>int</sub> − KEr<sub>int</sub> is the lateral kinetic energy (dotted green; drawn only where it exceeds 10<sup>−10</sup> KE<sub>int</sub>, below which the difference is round-off). Peak 1.4×10<sup>42</sup> erg at 10.7 d (the onset of convection), 1.3×10<sup>41</sup> erg at 0.5 d, lowest after 1 d 2.5×10<sup>39</sup> erg at 7.3 d, 1.1×10<sup>42</sup> erg now; KEr<sub>int</sub>/KE<sub>int</sub> = 0.476088 now. The dashed line is the paper's kinetic-energy level read from its Fig. 2 (~10<sup>43</sup> erg), a reference only.
c-fig4: This run starts from the paper's own IC, but with Ma's tables its Fe peak lies at 41.4 R<sub>☉</sub> (κ<sub>R</sub> 1.59, κ/κ<sub>Edd</sub> 0.89) at t = 0 and at 40.4 R<sub>☉</sub> (shell mean) at 20.59 d, so 40.6 R<sub>☉</sub> sits 0.2 R<sub>☉</sub> above the peak, not 1 R<sub>☉</sub> above it; the paper's 35 R<sub>☉</sub> is not reproduced by its own profile.
